**Emily Henry** (born May 17, 1991) is an American author who is best known for her 2020s romance novels _[Beach Read](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach_Read "Beach Read")_ , _[People We Meet on Vacation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_We_Meet_on_Vacation "People We Meet on Vacation")_ , _[Book Lovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_Lovers "Book Lovers")_ , _[Happy Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Place_\(novel\) "Happy Place \(novel\)")_ , _[Funny Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funny_Story_\(novel\) "Funny Story \(novel\)")_ , and _[Great Big Beautiful Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Big_Beautiful_Life "Great Big Beautiful Life")_ , all of which are [_New York Times_ bestsellers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Best_Seller_list "The New York Times Best Seller list").
## Biography
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Emily_Henry&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]
Henry was born on May 17, 1991.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-1) She attended [Lakota East High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakota_East_High_School "Lakota East High School") in [Liberty Township](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Township,_Butler_County,_Ohio "Liberty Township, Butler County, Ohio"), [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio"), then [Hope College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_College "Hope College") on a creative writing scholarship with plans to study dance.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-2) She also completed a writing residency at the now-defunct New York Center for Art & Media Studies, part of [Bethel University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethel_University_\(Minnesota\) "Bethel University \(Minnesota\)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-q1-3) She returned to Cincinnati after college; she currently lives and writes in Cincinnati and Northern [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky")'s [Ohio River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_River "Ohio River") region. As of 2016, she was a full-time writer and proofreader.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-q1-3)
## Writing career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Emily_Henry&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Writing career")]
Henry's debut [young adult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_adult_fiction "Young adult fiction") novel, _The Love That Split the World_ , was published in January 2016.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-Amazon_Author_Page-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-The_Interlochen_Review-5) After writing several young adult novels, her first adult romance novel, _[Beach Read](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach_Read "Beach Read"),_ was published in 2020, to widespread success.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-6) Henry's books have been featured in [BuzzFeed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuzzFeed "BuzzFeed"), _[O, The Oprah Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O,_The_Oprah_Magazine "O, The Oprah Magazine")_ , _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ , _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ , [The Skimm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Skimm "The Skimm"), and [Shondaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shondaland "Shondaland").
Henry continued to write adult romance novels. In 2021, _[People We Meet on Vacation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_We_Meet_on_Vacation "People We Meet on Vacation")_ was published. _[Book Lovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_Lovers "Book Lovers")_ was published in 2022 and _[Happy Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Place_\(novel\) "Happy Place \(novel\)")_ in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-7) _[Funny Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funny_Story_\(novel\) "Funny Story \(novel\)")_ was published in April 2024.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-8) Her sixth adult romance book, _[Great Big Beautiful Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Big_Beautiful_Life "Great Big Beautiful Life")_ , was published on April 22, 2025.
As of March 2023, Henry had sold more than 2.4 million books collectively.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-:0-9)
Writing for _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_\(website\) "Vulture \(website\)")_ in 2023, Allison P. Davis described Henry's books as containing elements of the [rom-com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") and [chick lit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_lit "Chick lit") genres and focusing on themes of "respect" as well as love.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-:0-9)
On September 23, 2026, Emily Henry officially announced her upcoming novel titled “[Modern Classic](https://www.penguin.co.uk/books/455134/modern-classic-by-henry-emily/9781405996006)” which is scheduled to be published on April 6th, 2027.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-10)
### On-screen adaptations
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Emily_Henry&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: On-screen adaptations")]
The first five of Henry's adult romance books have been optioned for on-screen adaptations.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-11)
In October 2022, a film adaptation of _People We Meet on Vacation_ by Sony's [3000 Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_Pictures "3000 Pictures") from a screenplay by Yulin Kuang was announced, with [Brett Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Haley "Brett Haley") directing and [Temple Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_Hill_Entertainment "Temple Hill Entertainment") producing.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-12) In September 2024, it was announced that [Tom Blyth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Blyth "Tom Blyth") and [Emily Bader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Bader "Emily Bader") would play Alex and Poppy. The movie was released on January 9, 2026.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-13) On April 5, 2023, it was announced that Kuang would also write and direct a film adaptation of _Beach Read_ for [20th Century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-14)
On March 28, 2023, a film adaptation of _Book Lovers_ by the production company [Tango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tango_Entertainment "Tango Entertainment") was announced, with [Sarah Heyward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Heyward "Sarah Heyward") attached to write the script.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-15) [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez")'s production company, [Nuyorican Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuyorican_Productions "Nuyorican Productions"), plans to develop _Happy Place_ into a film for Netflix.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-18)
Henry plans to write the film adaptation for _Funny Story_ herself.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Henry#cite_note-19)
